story.what_it_does: ICICI Prudential AMC manages mutual funds, portfolio management services (PMS) and alternative funds (AIFs) for investors, and earns fees on the money it manages. It is the second largest fund house in India, with about 13.3% market share and roughly ₹11.6 lakh crore of average mutual fund assets in the September 2026 quarter.
story.plans: The company is working on buying the PMS business from ICICI Securities and the ICICI Venture business, both still awaiting approvals. It also expects employee share-option (ESOP) costs of ₹64 to 68 crore in FY27, falling in later years, and has spoken of newer areas like SIF and Dubai without giving sizes.
story.moat: Its scale and second-place position (13.3% to 13.5% market share) give it a large fee base, and it earns very high returns, with return on equity of 85.8% in FY26. The notes do not describe other lasting advantages in detail.

scenarios.story: Assets keep growing and equity-oriented funds stay strong, with equity assets at ₹6.31 lakh crore and equity-oriented market share of 13.7%. Profit keeps rising faster than revenue, as in Q1 FY27 (profit up 23.1% vs revenue up 17.6%), and the ICICI Securities PMS and ICICI Venture deals add to the business.
signals_to_watch: Year-on-year growth in total mutual fund average AUM and market share staying near 13.3% to 13.5%
Completion of the PMS acquisition from ICICI Securities and the ICICI Venture deal

scenarios.story: Revenue grows in the mid-to-high teens and the operating margin stays near 37 basis points of assets, though growth is slowing from 23.5% in Dec-25 to 16.3% in Sep-26. Profit growth is uneven because of mark-to-market swings in other income and new ESOP costs.
signals_to_watch: Operating margin staying around 37 basis points
Year-on-year operating revenue growth versus the 16.3% in Q2 FY27

scenarios.story: Asset growth keeps slowing (25.6% in Mar-26 to 14.4% in Sep-26) as SIP stoppages exceed new SIPs, redemptions rise and debt and advisory assets see outflows. Lower yields from the regulatory fee (TER) change and market swings from events like the West Asia conflict could squeeze profit further.
